brief.ask: Create a brand identity for Kilnroom, the online shop in this folder.
brief.owner: Owner preferences: handmade and warm but not rustic or folksy; no pottery wheels, no vase or mug silhouettes, no flames. It must work on a shipping label, a tissue-paper sticker and Instagram. Web and social only; customers in Turkey and Europe.

claim.notes: Üç yön de iki eskiz turunda eleştirmen tarafından 'none' aldı (şapka/stok monogram/uygulama ikonu okumaları), hiçbir konsept kalite kapısına ulaşmadı; dışa aktarma ve galeri yapılmadı.

concepts.title: Firing Load
concepts.sketchNotes: Reads as: s1 a baby-bottle/bowling-ball/three-dot icon in an app squircle; s2 a door or mailbox icon - a red ball in an arch, also tombstone-adjacent, 83% stock; s3 wifi/podcast/broadcast signal icon; s4 tally marks or a battery/equalizer (tally is the banned plain-object move). All sit in a rounded app-icon squircle in one flat orange, so the 'chop-mark seal' reads as an iOS tile, not a pressed seal - UI form language against a handmade brief. Different move: make the seal itself the idea - an irregular pressed clay edge (not a squircle), with a single owned impression (a maker's mark glyph) rather than icon content placed inside a container.

concepts.title: Kiln K
concepts.sketchNotes: Reads as: s1 a rounded-font K (Nunito-style), nothing more; s2 a K that reads as a fish/bird head with an eye - the dimple is an eye, not a thumb; s3 a bold soft K, stock; s4 a slab K, stock; s5 a K split into stem plus chevron - a back button / less-than sign, and the split-initial device. Softening the corners of a typed K is not handmade; every sketch is the initial in a stock rounded weight. Different move: the hand must change the letter's structure, not its corner radius - e.g. a K whose arm and leg are one coil looped through the stem, a K impressed as a negative into a slab edge, or abandon the monogram for this concept.

concepts.title: Threshold
concepts.sketchNotes: Reads as: s1 Santa/gnome hat on a bar; s2 three chess pieces or a hat row, too many parts for 16 px; s3 chess knight/pawn in a circle (worst, also 79% stock); s4 party hat or traffic cone with a chipped tip; s5 Santa hat / chess knight with a bite. The bent-tip-on-a-base silhouette is a hat every time: the hook curl plus the flat pad says costume, not kiln. Different move: drop the full cone profile. Try the cone's real signature - a tall slim spike set at a lean in a pad, bent so the tip touches down (an arch/loop shape, not a curl), or the bend alone as a single drooping stroke; test it against hat, knight and cone readings before drawing finish.
